questions_and_answers.question: When does a verb in Hindi agree with its subject?

answers.answer: Only when the subject is in the oblique case
When the subject is in the direct case
Only when the object is in the direct case

questions_and_answers.question: In the sentence 'मुझको किताबें चाहिए थीं', why is the verb in the feminine plural form?

answers.answer: Because the subject is feminine plural
Because the object 'किताबें' is feminine plural
Because verbs never agree with subjects

questions_and_answers.question: What happens to the verb if the subject is in the oblique case and there is no direct case noun?

answers.answer: The verb agrees with the subject
The verb takes neutral masculine singular form
The verb agrees with any object

questions_and_answers.question: Which of the following correctly translates 'आपको क्या चाहिए था?'?
In 'मेरे दोस्त हिन्दी बोलते थे', why does the verb agree in masculine plural?

answers.answer: Because 'दोस्त' is masculine plural in direct case
Because the verb always agrees with the first noun

questions_and_answers.question: Which sentence conveys past necessity or obligation?

articles.text:
The addition of 'था' (thā) gives a past meaning to 'चाहिए'. For example, 'आना चाहिए था' means someone should have come, 'कोशिश करनी चाहिए थी' means one should have tried, and 'मुझे नौकरी चाहिए थी' means I needed a job.
In Hindi, the verb agrees with its subject when the subject is in the direct case. For instance, 'मेरे दोस्त हिन्दी बोलते थे' means 'My friends used to speak Hindi'; here both the subject and verb are in the masculine plural form.
If the subject is in the oblique case, the verb cannot agree with it. Instead, the verb may agree with a direct case noun if one is present. An example is 'मुझको किताबें चाहिए थीं', meaning 'I needed the books'; the verb agrees with the feminine plural noun 'किताबें'.
When no direct case noun is available, the verb reverts to its neutral form, masculine singular. For example, 'आपको क्या चाहिए था?' translates to 'What did you want?'.
Some useful indefinite expressions include: 'कुछ न कुछ' meaning 'something or other', 'कोई न कोई' meaning 'somebody or other', and 'कभी न कभी' meaning 'sometime or other'.
